answer: One workable design: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because summit only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, bridge is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any reef approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
